findings.detail: All three provider families now require successful terminal dispatch, valid measured usage, and no retries. Explicit failures and malformed receipts classify the arm as infrastructure failure.

Inherited pair reporting stops shared campaign health and preserves raw costs, preventing subsequent arms and queued tasks. Accounted-result persistence retains classification when the original result file differs; no frozen ancestor is changed.

Classification runs at arm completion/throw, not as a new transport interception. Already running concurrent work is governed by existing shared pre-dispatch guards; this wrapper does not retroactively cancel requests or establish remote settlement.

timeout_assessment.evidence: One failed request tokenizer among 181, configured 30s timeout and coordinator-reported 40.6s observed elapsed. This supports a bounded operational timeout hypothesis, not certainty that service latency caused the failure.
requirements: Declare any timeout change prospectively and identically for eager/control and demand/treatment.
Retain single transport attempt, fixed request/token ceilings and whole-arm/run deadlines; account for increased maximum waiting in cancellation drain.
Keep the shared-health correction regardless of timeout selection.
Preserve R1 failure and all known/unknown costs; no output-based policy tuning or replacement of failed evidence.
